claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child does not live with claimant and weekly upkeep (£10.00) is below the Child Benefit rate (£26.05)
  - Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child/children.

**How old is the child (or the youngest child if you have more than one) that you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
- How old is your child?
- Or which age range: under 16, 16-19, or 20 or over?

This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex - he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the automatic qualification category. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I'm guessing he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this to proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. So Alex is not in paid work and is in primary school. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any certain benefits in his own right:

**Is Alex NOT receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name?**

(Again, for an 8-year-old in primary school, I'd expect the answer to be "yes" - meaning he's not receiving these benefits - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - no, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a normal 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given that he's 8 years old and in primary school, I'm assuming the answer is no, but I need to confirm this to move forward.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that could qualify you for Child Benefit:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the main criterion for most people
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself and your family
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Could you tell me which of these situations applies to you? The most common one is simply that you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live here with my family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the main residency requirement satisfied. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. There are a few ways this could work:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - You have him living in your home
2. **You're contributing to his upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (or more) towards his care, including things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents
3. **You're paying maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers his upkeep and equals or exceeds the Child Benefit amount

I'm guessing the first one applies - that Alex lives with you - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum. But I do help out with some money for things like clothes and bits and pieces for school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. So Alex lives with his mum, but you contribute financially to his upkeep. That's helpful information.

To proceed, I need to clarify a bit more about your financial contributions:

**Are your contributions to Alex's care (clothes, school items, etc.) at least equal to the amount of Child Benefit you would receive for him?**

For context, the current Child Benefit rates are:
- £23.80 per week for the first child
- £15.80 per week for each additional child

So that would be roughly £100+ per month for a first child, or £65+ per month for an additional child.

Are your regular contributions at least this amount, either weekly, monthly, or in lump sum payments?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I give about £10 a week to help out with things for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that. Based on what you've told me, you're contributing £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which works out to roughly £40-43 per month.

Unfortunately, this appears to be below the Child Benefit threshold, which is £23.80 per week (approximately £100+ per month) for a first child. For you to qualify under the "contributing to upkeep" path, your contributions would need to be at least equal to the Child Benefit amount.

Let me navigate through the system to confirm this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your situation, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit eligibility requires that you either:
1. Live with the child, OR
2. Pay at least the Child Benefit amount towards their upkeep (£23.80 per week for a first child), OR
3. Pay maintenance under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds the Child Benefit amount

In your case:
- You don't live with Alex (he lives with his mum)
- You contribute £10 per week, which is less than the required £23.80 per week threshold
- There's no court order or formal maintenance agreement in place

**What you could do:**

1. **Speak to Alex's mum** - If you could formalize a maintenance arrangement (through a court order or agreement) that covers his upkeep at the required level, this might change the situation. You'd then need to reapply.

2. **Speak to HMRC** - If you believe your circumstances might have changed or if there are other factors I haven't considered, you can contact HMRC directly at the Child Benefit office for further advice.

3. **Check if the mum is claiming** - Alex's mother (who he lives with) should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, as she meets the responsibility requirement.

Is there anything else you'd like to discuss about this, or any other children you'd like to check eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. So because I'm only contributing £10 a week and he doesn't live with me, I'm not eligible. That's disappointing, but I understand. No, that was just for Alex - he's my only child. Thank you for checking this for me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome, and I'm sorry it wasn't the outcome you were hoping for. You've understood it correctly – the key issue is that your contributions of £10 per week fall below the required threshold of £23.80 per week for the first child, and since Alex doesn't live with you, you don't meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit.

However, it's good that you're supporting Alex financially, even if it doesn't meet the Child Benefit criteria. If your situation changes in the future – for example, if Alex were to live with you, or if you were able to increase your contributions to meet the threshold, or if a formal maintenance arrangement were put in place – you'd be welcome to reapply.

Let me formally record this outcome for you:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for using this service. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or need help with anything else, feel free to ask. All the best with Alex!
